data.narrative:
Performance Drone Works, a Series B-stage autonomous systems company founded by Ryan Gury, has raised $110M+ to date. The broader Drones & Autonomous sector includes eight private peers—among them Elroy Air, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, and Archer Aviation—though no public comparables exist in this subsector.

Valuation analysis is constrained by limited peer data at the same stage and valuation tier. A Peer-Median approach proved inapplicable; the sector contains only one same-stage comparable, insufficient to establish a reliable median. Consequently, valuation rests on Stage-Progression methodology, which applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage rounds against the $110M total-raised proxy. This yields an implied valuation of $209M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $178M (low) to $240M (high), with a median point estimate of $209M. The narrow methodological foundation reflects genuine data scarcity rather than analytical rigor; only one quantitative anchor is available. Key uncertainties include the applicability of standard stage-progression multiples to frontier-stage drone technology, capital intensity relative to peers, and whether the $110M proxy accurately represents fair-value entry points. A Peer-Median cross-check would substantially strengthen conviction once additional same-stage or adjacent-stage private comparables reach disclosure.
